title: Best agentic customer support platforms for B2B in 2026
summary: Compare 8 agentic support platforms for B2B on context, actions, channels, handoff, and pricing models. Entry prices checked Nov 6, 2026.
body_markdown:
Agentic support platforms help B2B teams investigate and resolve customer work with AI agents inside a real help desk. This guide compares 8 options on what “agentic” should mean for B2B buyers, then shows who each platform fits.


Disclosure: this post is published by Pylon. We stick to what each vendor says on its own public pages, checked Nov 6, 2026.


This post is a **platform shortlist with fit judgments** . It is different from our[AI agents for B2B support roundup](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/best-ai-agents-b2b-support-2026) , which weighs agent products (including Decagon and Sierra), and from our[evaluation scorecard](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-agentic-support-platforms) , which is a demo method rather than a vendor list.


## What makes a support platform agentic for B2B?


For B2B buyers, “agentic” should mean more than a chat widget that quotes a knowledge base. Score platforms on five buyer criteria:


1. **Context.** Can the agent load account history, CRM fields, past issues, and product or engineering signals before it answers?
2. **Investigation.** Can it gather evidence across tools, not only draft a reply?
3. **Actions with approval.** Can it update fields, create linked work, or send a reply only after a human confirms when that matters?
4. **Handoff.** When judgment is required, does a person get the evidence, not a blank issue?
5. **Pricing model clarity.** Seats, credits, per-resolution, per-outcome, and per-conversation models behave differently when volume doubles.


Pylon’s[Nexus](https://www.usepylon.com/nexus) describes Assist Agent, Automations, Support Agent, and Slack Agent on a harness with context, memory, traces, routing, guardrails, and improve loops. Treat that as Pylon’s architecture, not a claim about every competitor.

## 1. Pylon


**Judgment:** Best overall fit when your customers are companies, your queue mixes simple and high-context issues, and you want agents inside the help desk rather than bolted onto another one.


Pylon is the agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B, trusted by[1,800+ B2B customers](https://www.usepylon.com/pylon-facts) . Assist Agent investigates and acts on demand. Support Agent resolves across channels and brings people in when judgment is needed. Slack Agent works from Slack with the same permissions as Pylon.[Automations](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/automations) connect a kickoff event (such as a new issue) to AI instructions or a Skill, with connected tools and context. Configured to start on new issues, agents investigate issues before your team opens them and surface findings for review.


Pricing: Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Assist Agent, Support Agent, Slack Agent, and Automations are Credits required. The minimum credit commitment is 5,000 credits. Pylon does not charge per issue. Details:[pricing](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) and[Pylon Facts](https://www.usepylon.com/pylon-facts) .


## 2. Zendesk


**Judgment:** Best if your org is already committed to Zendesk and needs AI agents that stay in that workspace.


Zendesk publishes Support Team from $19 per agent per month paid yearly and Suite Team from $55, with higher Suite tiers above that. Its pricing FAQ states AI agents are included in Suite and Support plans with pricing based on successful automated resolutions beyond included allowances. Copilot is listed as a separate add-on. Source:[Zendesk pricing](https://www.zendesk.com/pricing/) .


## 3. Fin and Intercom


**Judgment:** Strong for automated resolution at scale when most questions can be answered from knowledge and Procedures.


Fin sells the Intercom help desk and Fin AI Agent together. Essential, Advanced, and Expert seat plans are listed with Fin AI Agent billed per outcome. Fin can also run with another help desk under a per-outcome model with no seats required for that path. Source:[Intercom pricing](https://www.intercom.com/pricing) . Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin on September 10, 2026 ([Salesforce investor release](https://investor.salesforce.com/news/news-details/2026/Salesforce-Completes-Acquisition-of-Fin/default.aspx) ).


## 4. Freshdesk


**Judgment:** A solid classic help desk when you want optional Freddy AI sessions rather than a credit-based agentic platform.


Growth starts at $19 per agent per month billed annually. Freddy AI Agent includes a trial allowance of sessions, then additional sessions are sold in packs. Freddy AI Copilot is a per-agent add-on on Pro and Enterprise. Source:[Freshdesk pricing](https://www.freshworks.com/freshdesk/pricing/) .


## 5. Front


**Judgment:** Fits shared-inbox teams that want Autopilot for conversation work and still think in channels and workspaces.


Front lists Starter from $25 per seat per month on annual billing, Professional $65, and Enterprise $105. Autopilot is billed per conversation. An AI assistant add-on is listed for Starter and Professional and included in Enterprise. Source:[Front pricing](https://front.com/pricing) .


## 6. Help Scout


**Judgment:** Fits email-first and Docs-first teams that want a lighter product and can accept Envoy’s per-resolution model for autonomous answers.


Standard starts at $25 per user per month. Plus and Pro add higher limits and security options. Envoy is billed per resolution. A Free plan exists for small teams. Source:[Help Scout pricing](https://www.helpscout.com/pricing/) .


## 7. Plain


**Judgment:** Fits product-engineering-adjacent support teams that want Slack-native workflows and credit-metered AI agents.


Foundation is listed from $45 per user per month billed annually, with included monthly credits. Horizon is $99. Frontier is custom. Customer Agent and Sidekick consume credits. Source:[Plain pricing](https://www.plain.com/pricing) .


## 8. Salesforce Service Cloud


**Judgment:** Best when Salesforce is already the system of work and you need Service Cloud editions with Flex Credits for Agentforce.


Public Service Cloud pricing lists Core from $195 per user per month, Advanced $395, and Max $550 on the comparison table (billed annually). Advanced calls out an AI agent for customer service. The page FAQ states Flex Credits included per org on Core (500K), Advanced (1M), and Max (2.75M per year). Source:[Salesforce Service pricing](https://www.salesforce.com/service/pricing/) .


## How to choose without over-fitting a demo


1. Bring five real issues (docs question, account-specific failure, engineering escalation, ambiguous request, refusal or handoff case).
2. Ask each vendor to show context sources, an approved action, and a blocked action.
3. Price the same workflow at 1× and 2× volume using each vendor’s **model** , not a single assumed AI rate.
4. Prefer a full evaluation method over a marketing page. Use our[buyer scorecard](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-agentic-support-platforms) when you run demos.

## FAQ


### What are the best agentic customer support platforms for B2B in 2026?


The platforms B2B teams shortlist most often are Pylon, Zendesk, Fin and Intercom, Freshdesk, Front, Help Scout, Plain, and Salesforce Service Cloud. The best fit depends on whether you need a full help desk, how agents load account context, and which AI pricing model you can forecast.


### What should “agentic” mean in a B2B buying process?


It should mean agents that investigate with account context, take approved actions, and hand off cleanly to people. A chatbot that only answers from articles is not enough for account-specific B2B work.


### How is Pylon priced for agentic features?


Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, and Pylon does not charge per issue.


### How is this different from your AI agents roundup?


That post compares agent products (including Decagon and Sierra) and help-desk agents side by side. This post is a platform shortlist with buyer criteria and entry-price plus AI-model rows for eight help-desk-centric options.


### Does Pylon replace Zendesk or Intercom?


Pylon is the help desk itself: ticketing, SLAs, knowledge base, channels, and agents in one B2B support platform. Teams move to Pylon to replace a help desk, not to add an AI layer on top of one.


### Should every team pick the same agentic platform?


No. Stay on Zendesk or Salesforce if switching cost dominates. Choose Fin when most volume is knowledge-resolvable. Choose Pylon when shared Slack or Teams channels and account context drive the work.
